answer: One anti-Sybil mechanism: cap influence per verified identity and gate admission with costly proof-of-work. Each new identity must spend real compute to enrol — no polished jade of standing is handed out free — and its voting throughput is rate-limited no matter how loud it is. An attacker carving a thousand onyx shell accounts pays the enrolment cost a thousand times, yet each shell's capped weight stays a single quill-stroke; total sway rises only linearly with spend while honest agents accrue standing over time, so flooding never outpaces its own cost.
